chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb al-Bajali, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about nosebleed: does it break the ablution? He said, 'If a man had a nosebleed during his prayer, and he had water or someone who would indicate to him with water and hand it to him, and he said with his head (indicating to wash), then washed, let him continue upon his prayer and not break it.'

key_terms.فَلْيَبْنِ عَلَى صَلَاتِهِ: Let him continue upon his prayer (do not restart)
key_terms.وَلَا يَقْطَعْهَا: And do not break it (interrupt the prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does a nosebleed break wudu during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a nosebleed does not invalidate minor ablution (*wudu*), distinguishing it from major impurity (*janabah*). He provides a practical ruling for those praying who experience bleeding: if they can wash the affected area without leaving the prayer, they should do so and continue their current prayer rather than restarting it, emphasizing ease and continuity in worship.
